headline: Canadian Farm-Tariff Notice Has 35% Chance by 31 October
deck: Foreman puts 35% odds on a U.S. record naming eligible Canadian-linked agricultural products and their effective date by 31 October.
body: Maine Senator Susan Collins said she had secured additional tariff exemptions for products important to her state’s blueberry, potato, apple and seaweed producers. The Wall Street Journal, as reported by CityNews, said a White House proclamation changing tariffs on certain agricultural and forestry products could come as early as Friday. [E1][E2][E3]

For now, the published tariff record is Canada’s countermeasure: its Finance Department says the measure took effect on 8 September and matches the U.S. rate for the same goods targeted by the U.S. measures. [E4]

The underlying dispute remains substantial. AP reported that after trade negotiations collapsed in August, President Donald Trump imposed 50% tariffs on about $20 billion in Canadian goods and Canada retaliated. [E5]

The paper’s 22 October coverage tracked Canada and Ontario’s response to the tariff dispute. What has changed is the reported prospect of targeted U.S. relief, though its legal terms have not been published.

**The desk's reading.** The chance that an official U.S. record will name eligible Canadian-linked agricultural products and an effective date by 31 October is 35%. I start from a 50% desk prior: the reported possible Friday proclamation and Collins’s statement that exemptions will be granted point toward YES. [E1][E2] I move the probability down because the report is conditional and the senator’s announcement is preliminary evidence of a policy outcome. The strongest competing reading is that the reported White House action will arrive promptly and make the details routine. That remains possible, but the two reports leave meaningful room for the deadline to pass without a qualifying official record.

**The next test.** The call settles YES only if, by 31 October, an official U.S. tariff schedule, proclamation or implementing notice names eligible Canadian-linked agricultural products and an effective date. It settles NO if no such record is published by then; a statement without both terms does not qualify.
